paper.title_en: The role of complementarity and quantum correlation in the uncertainty relations and the optimum states
paper.abstract_en: Uncertainty relations are used in quantum mechanics to illustrate the complementarity of two observables, assuming there is a lower bound for the product of their dispersions that depends on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation of those observables in an optimum state. In this work, we demonstrate that the complex parameter of the optimum state equation has real and imaginary parts that depend on the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation between the observables in the optimum state, respectively. We apply our results to a two-level system, finding that the first-order quantum correlation and the commutation relation of two spin-1/2 projections in the optimum state complement each other and, finally, when the term correlation is used, a lower bound for the uncertainty principle does not depend on any parameter of the optimum state, in contrast to the usual form of the Heisenberg principle.
